decisions.label: Where models live
decisions.value: Model classes are nested in the family's class body; declaration order by level is today's ladder order. A rung declared later joins its base's family, so nothing is silently dropped (checked: adding Dahl gives 15 models and M3.dahl appears in the derived record).

decisions.label: Additivity rules
decisions.value: Checked when the class is created: changing an inherited unit or definition raises, shadowing a parameter with None raises, loosening a required one raises, a parameter named after an API attribute or a type alias raises, and reusing an inherited definition under a new name raises. The only change allowed is `x = Parameter()` (optional below, required from this rung on). The family also refuses two different definitions of one name on different branches.

decisions.label: One source
decisions.value: Model.rung() and Family.v1_ladder() derive today's Ladder; it equals ladders()["integrated_servo"] as a whole record. Aliases, packed and deployment names are still imported from today's module.

decisions.label: Values
decisions.value: Parameter is a descriptor: on the class it is the Parameter, on an instance the float. Instances are frozen. A fit leaves parameters its log cannot see unset instead of inventing them.

decisions.label: Generic fit
decisions.value: A recording terms dict shows what the physics reads. Parameters that are read and move the log (checked at a jittered point) are fitted, seeded from their unit plus the start value. Levenberg–Marquardt runs in log space so signs are kept. Anything the log can't identify becomes a skip with a reason.

decisions.label: Vectorized predict
decisions.value: Today's model.py is loaded a second time with numpy in place of math and _sign, and checked against the stdlib run on three samples every call. If numpy can't run it (LuGre), it falls back to a loop. 100k samples take about 3 ms.

decisions.label: Selection
decisions.value: Ladder order, the lowest rung within 1.5× the pooled within-plateau noise floor, or None. It no longer requires a single fallback chain, so the black box competes.

decisions.label: Black box
decisions.value: BlackBox base with a degree-3 polynomial per direction (8 weights, lstsq), standing in for today's MLP. It extends no physics rung.

built.best_when: A type's models are refinements of each other and the people adding rungs write Python. You get one class to read (parameters with units, equation, references, physics) and plain value objects that hand straight to MuJoCo (m3.mujoco()) or sim2real (m3.values(), canonical SI names).
built.loses_when: You want one object for 'this servo': here it's several fitted instances plus a FamilyFit (v7's thesis). You want values as storable, diffable data (v8). You need constructor keywords checked statically: types come only through descriptor overloads, the 33 injected M1 fields are invisible to a checker, and none of this is verified with pyright, which isn't installed here. The core is large (546 lines). Ties between equally good siblings fall to declaration order.
keep_parts: v1_ladder(): derive today's Ladder from the classes and assert it equals ladders() as a whole record. This makes 'one source' checkable and makes migration a one-line change.
Additivity enforced when the class is created, with `x = Parameter()` as the only way to tighten an inherited parameter, plus reserved API names and the alias check.

Generic fitting: a recording terms dict finds what the physics reads, seeds come from units, and unidentifiable parameters become a skip with a reason. Plus the numpy-swapped reference run, cross-checked against the scalar run.
built.migration: Now it is additive: src/, the v1 ruler, robotparts' vendored model.py/model.json bytes and sim2real are untouched, and the classes read today's rung code by path. Later, actuators/servo/ladder.py becomes `LADDER = IntegratedServo.v1_ladder()`, with ALIASES/PACKED/DEPLOYMENT moved verbatim into the family body. Because the derived record already equals today's, ladders(), the ruler tests, sim2real's parity test and robotparts' vendoring should keep passing; the scenario's equality check backs this, but I didn't run those suites against the swap. Worth adding to the parity test: SELECT_LIMIT == TWINNED_LIMIT. The other 11 types can move one at a time.
built.new_rung_cost: One nested class: docstring title, new Parameter(unit, definition) lines, equation and references. To make it runnable, add actuators/rungs/<word>/model.py and model.json. There is no record, no seeds() override and no registry; fit, family fit, select_best, the tree and the derived v1 record pick it up automatically. The frozen ruler's key list would fail on purpose, because a new rung is a ruler change.
built.simulated: The rig log is the fixture's simulated plateau sweep, and M1 comes from the fixture's illustrative datasheet. Runnable: M0–M3 using their reference model.py; M3.lugre runs only at steady state and the fit skips it. M3.load and M4.ripple need inputs the log lacks. M3.weakening_capture, M4.drivetrain, M5.*, and M6 are declared only. M7 is a numpy polynomial standing in for the MLP. The fit frees only required parameters (stribeck_exponent stays at 2) and reports no uncertainty. On servo A, M2's viscous_friction ends on the positivity bound (≈0). tree().show() writes integrated_servo_tree.html with mermaid 10.9.1 loaded from a CDN; I rendered it headlessly and looked at it.

decisions.label: Parameter
decisions.value: A frozen-dataclass descriptor: on the class it is the record (unit, definition, required); on an instance it is the float. Typed, so servo[Stribeck].breakaway_torque is a float

decisions.label: Additive enforcement
decisions.value: __init_subclass__ allows a rung to add parameters or promote optional to required. Removing, redeclaring, demoting, aliased names and unknown names all raise before the class registers

decisions.label: One source
decisions.value: A rung registers when its class is declared; as_ladder() builds the v1 Ladder (v1's own checks run on it); ladder_diff == []

decisions.label: Runnable
decisions.value: Only a rung that defines its own torque runs; an inherited torque never runs under a child's name

decisions.label: Physics
decisions.value: Vectorized numpy torque on each class, held to the stdlib model.py by parity() (max difference 0.0)

decisions.label: Fitting
decisions.value: One generic Levenberg-Marquardt. Starting values come from each parameter's unit, not the rung: a torque starts at the median |tau|, a damping at 0, a speed scale gets 6 starts and is fitted as its log. No per-rung seeds

decisions.label: Hybrid methods
decisions.value: fit/ladder/tree/describe work on the class (browse, or a fresh instance) and on an instance (its values)

decisions.label: Black box
decisions.value: M7.learned is a per-direction RBF ridge regression with 14 weights, standing in for the MLP; same interface, competes in select_best

decisions.label: show()

built.best_when: The thing you carry is a servo, not a model: sim2real twins a unit, a fleet is a list of units, and each unit says which rung its own data paid for (A -> M3, B -> M2 from the same datasheet). The batch fit's status table answers 'what happened to every model' in one place.
built.loses_when: You want values as plain data to diff, store or share without their unit. A unit is a mutable object graph that fit changes in place (v8's Parameters sets win there). Each unit also builds all 14 instances, hybrid class/instance methods are one more idea to learn, and the core is over its line budget (473 vs 350).
keep_parts: Parameter as a descriptor: the record on the class, the value on an instance, typed for type checkers
Additive vocabulary enforced in __init_subclass__, plus as_ladder()/ladder_diff deriving and checking the v1 Ladder from the classes
Generic fitting with starting values by parameter unit (speed scales fitted as their log), plus 'runnable = defines its own torque'
built.migration: Each Rung(...) record in actuators/servo/ladder.py becomes a class, and LADDER = IntegratedServo.as_ladder() keeps ladders(), fallback() and parameters() working, along with robotparts' vendored rung folders (untouched) and sim2real's parity test. ladder_diff == [] is the guard that proves the swap changed nothing. rungs/*/model.py stays as the stdlib ruler; the numpy torque is checked against it by parity in a test. built.new_rung_cost: One class: Parameters, a docstring (the title), equation, references, code if the package has its physics, and a vectorized torque only if it should run. It then appears automatically in models, ladder, tree, as_ladder, every unit, the batch fit and select_best. No seeds() override, no registry, no second record.

built.migration: Purely additive; nothing in src/ changes until a variant is picked. servo.py would replace servo/ladder.py's VOCABULARY and RUNGS, and LADDER would become IntegratedServo.as_ladder(). ladders(), the v1 ruler, robotparts' vendored rung bytes and sim2real's parity test would keep reading the same Ladder; drift() returns [] today. discover() would also need to look for ModelFamily subclasses.
built.new_rung_cost: One class: Parameter declarations, a docstring title, equation and references, and optionally a numpy torque(p, v) with code= to check it against model.py. It registers itself when defined, even outside the family body. There is no Rung record, no seeds() override and no registry. I checked this outside the scenario: a Tanh rung showed up in as_ladder(), fit and select_best with no other edit. An alias-named parameter (sigma2), a clashing redeclaration and a drifted equation were each refused, and the family stayed at 14 models.
built.simulated: Rig logs come from fixture.py's simulated plateaus, and the servo is illustrative. Physics runs only for M0, M1, M2, M3.stribeck and M7.learned; M3.load needs tau_load and M3.lugre needs state, so both are declared without physics, as is everything above M3. M7.learned is a numpy stand-in for the MLP: a per-direction linear model on [1, |v|, ln|v|, ln²|v|]. Not built: a .pyi stub, a discover() change, and runs of robotparts or sim2real. judges.hinge: For a maintainer, v6 wins mainly because it keeps one copy of the physics: it runs today's model.py on numpy arrays and its derived Ladder equals today's byte for byte. v7 and v8 retype the physics in numpy and silently drop rung notes, and the v1 ruler does not notice either, because it compares sets and does not check prose. If retyped-but-parity-checked physics is acceptable, and if storable or diffable value sets are weighted at all (they are not one of fr1–fr6), v8 closes most of the gap. Its remaining loss is fr6, because type checkers cannot see the generated Parameters fields.
